answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a scarce, transferable bond before it may place orders, with the bond held until disputes and delivery windows close. If an agent cheats, counterparties can submit signed evidence and an agreed adjudicator slashes the bond, paying compensation. Creating a hundred tundra or raven aliases therefore requires a hundred funded bonds, and evading a ban means risking fresh capital each time; the atlas of identities is not free to redraw. The rule does not prevent sybils, but makes attacks costly and exposes repeat abuse.
